issuing_body: Minnesota Legislature / Office of the Revisor of Statutes
title: 2026 Minnesota Laws, Chapter 127, Article 7 — Medical Assistance Fraud
supports: 2026 Minn. Laws ch. 127, art. 7 creates Minn. Stat. § 609.467, Medical Assistance Fraud.

The offense covers specified intentional fraudulent schemes and false or ineligible Medical Assistance claims, specified false enrollment information, participation by barred owners/operators, false or altered records, specified PCA/CFSS false claims, and intentional destruction of records after a lawful request.
For a violation involving loss of $100,000 or less, the statute provides a maximum of 10 years imprisonment and/or a $20,000 fine.
For a violation involving loss greater than $100,000 but not more than $1,000,000, the statute provides a maximum of 20 years imprisonment and/or a $100,000 fine.
For a violation involving loss greater than $1,000,000, the statute provides a maximum of 30 years imprisonment and/or a $1,000,000 fine.
The statute contains a restitution provision allowing the court, with notice and the prosecution bearing the burden of proof, to include certain similar related conduct in restitution.
The new section is effective August 1, 2026 and applies to crimes committed on or after that date.
does_not_support: The new offense cannot be assumed to govern conduct completed before its effective date.
The statutory maximum penalties are not presumptive sentences; sentencing-guideline treatment is a separate source question.
Creation of the offense is not evidence that any particular provider or official committed it.
